newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-JUVENTUS OLD BOYS READY FOR OLD CLUB.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-JUVENTUS OLD BOYS READY FOR OLD CLUB.

text.p: Borussia Dortmund will know exactly what to expect from Juventus in the European Cup final on May 28 as almost half the team used to play for them.

Juergen Kohler, Andreas Moeller, Julio Cesar, Paulo Sousa and Stefan Reuter will all be eager to get the better of their old club -- while Matthias Sammer (ex-Inter Milan) and Karlheinz Reidle (ex-Lazio) also have first-hand knowledge of serie A.
The German club face a daunting task in Munich against the reigning champions, who reached the final for the second successive season beating Ajax 4-1 on Wednesday for a 6-2 aggregate victory.
Dortmund secured their place by beating Manchester United 1-0 at Old Trafford to follow up the 1-0 win in their Westfalenstadion two weeks ago.
Juventus also beat United 1-0 at home and away earlier in the competition so in that respect the two teams approach the final as equals.

But in almost every other respect, Dortmund go in as underdogs and will have to produce something extraordinary to emulate Bayern Munich (1974-75-76) and Hamburg (1983) and bring Europe's most prestigious club trophy back to Germany for the first time in 14 years.
Dortmund will be bidding to win their first European trophy since lifting the Cup Winners' Cup in 1966.
"In any game of 90 minutes you always have a chance, even if you happen to be playing Juventus, the best team in the world," said Dortmund coach Ottmar Hitzfeld after his team's victory.
"We have won four and drawn one of our five away matches in the Champions League this season and I am optimistic for the final."

Dortmund, missing five internationals including European Footballer of the Year Sammer, survived a battering from United at Old Trafford to reach their first European final since losing, coincidentally, to Juventus in the UEFA Cup in 1993.
Julio Cesar, Kohler and Moeller all played for Juve against Dortmund as they won 6-1 on aggregate.

United had 21 goal attempts, six clearcut scoring chances and two "goals" disallowed, but could find no way past the Dortmund defence which was marshalled superbly by Kohler, returning to the ground where he sustained an injury playing for Germany in their opening match of Euro'96 which put him out for the rest of the tournament.
"It was very nice coming back here and winning after what happened last summer," said man-of-the-match Kohler afterwards.
"United gave us a lot of problems, but we showed that we are a very hard team to beat."
Dortmund took the lead after only eight minutes when 20-year-old Lars Ricken outpaced the flat-footed United defence and fired a left-foot shot into the far corner of Peter Schmeichel's net.
Following Rene Tretschok's first-leg goal in Germany, it meant United had to score at least three times to win -- and despite creating so may chances, they failed to take any of them.

Dortmund defended resolutely for long periods, soaking up sustained United pressure, and although United manager Alex Ferguson said he was unimpressed with their organisation, the English side failed to score against them in the 180 minutes of the tie.

For United the night was a huge disappointment, ending hopes that they could win the European Cup for the first time since 1968 in the city which claimed the lives of eight of the Busby Babes in 1958.
"I have a clear vision of the future and we will do better next season," said Ferguson afterwards.
But on Wednesday night, the immediate future looked brighter for Borussia -- for the next five weeks at least.
